s1.syndrome_frame: Hypertension with multisystem involvement and hemorrhagic stroke
salient_findings: Hypertension first noted at age 24 during pregnancy
Basal ganglia hemorrhage at age 38
Splenomegaly of unknown cause at age 21
Normochromic microcytic anemia and thrombocytopenia
Bilateral adrenal lesions
Hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins
key_facts: Hypertension first noted at age 24 during pregnancy
Family history of similar splenomegaly finding in younger brother
Hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins on CT
No symptoms of adrenal hormone excess
Blood pressure controlled on a single antihypertensive agent

shortlist.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar splenomegaly finding and presence of hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of bilateral adrenal lesions and history of hypertension

shortlist.label: Primary aldosteronism
shortlist.why_kept: Hypertension and presence of bilateral adrenal lesions

shortlist.label: Cushing's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of bilateral adrenal lesions and hypertension

shortlist.label: Familial adrenal pathologies
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar splenomegaly finding and presence of bilateral adrenal lesions

shortlist.label: Portal vein thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins

shortlist.label: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of bilateral adrenal lesions and family history of similar splenomegaly finding

raw.rationale: The patient's history of basal ganglia hemorrhage, splenomegaly, and family history of similar splenomegaly finding, along with the presence of hepatosplenomegaly and dilated portal and splenic veins, are consistent with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, which is characterized by vascular dysplasias and telangiectasias that can lead to hemorrhage and organ dysfunction.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: No symptoms of adrenal hormone excess and normal urinary metanephrines

rejected.label: Primary aldosteronism
rejected.why: Normal aldosterone-renin ratio and controlled blood pressure on a single antihypertensive agent

rejected.label: Cushing's syndrome
rejected.why: No symptoms of adrenal hormone excess and normal cortisol levels

rejected.label: Familial adrenal pathologies
rejected.why: Bilateral adrenal lesions are present but do not explain the patient's other findings

rejected.label: Portal vein thrombosis
rejected.why: Dilated portal and splenic veins are present, but there is no evidence of thrombosis

rejected.label: Splenic vein thrombosis
rejected.why: Dilated splenic vein is present, but there is no evidence of thrombosis

rejected.label: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
rejected.why: No other characteristic findings such as retinal angiomas, cerebellar hemangioblastomas, or clear cell renal carcinomas
